papers.title_in_file: The Zeno Blockade - Quantum Computing Inc
papers.version_note: A company educational web page; navigation menu text precedes the article and the links and animation are not in the text layer.
papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc lesson page that explains, with Hamiltonians and verbal arguments, how a Zeno blockade lets one photon block another from entering a nonlinear cavity.

assertions.value: The authors name the effect of making two photons bounce off each other the Zeno blockade.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, introduction
quotes: make two photons bounce off each other, an effect known as the Zeno blockade
assertions.certainty_reason: The page defines the term in its introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that anything that removes, or changes the sign of, quantum probability amplitude can lead to a Zeno effect, and that this can happen in many ways.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, refresher section
quotes: Anything that removes, (or changes the sign of) quantum probability amplitude can lead to a Zeno effect
quantum amplitude has to build up, unlike classical probability
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives its own papers as the support but the links are not in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Zeno blockade is a key ingredient to quantum computing and could be used to construct quantum logic gates.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, introduction
quotes: The Zeno blockade is a key ingredient to quantum computing and could be used to construct quantum logic gates

assertions.value: The authors state that the Zeno blockade is not quite how the company uses it in its technology, that it still plays a key role, and that it could be used that way in future devices.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, introduction
quotes: While this isn't quite how we use it in our technology, it still plays a key role, and could be used that way in future devices.

assertions.value: The authors state that light can stay in a region of space for a long time if it fits a full number of wavelengths, a condition they call resonance, and that a cavity can be resonant with several frequencies of light at the same time.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Optical Cavity
quotes: it can stay in a region of space for a long time if it happens to nicely fit a full number of wavelengths (a condition known as resonance)
Cavities can also be resonant with multiple different frequencies of light at the same time
assertions.certainty_reason: The page defines resonance in the Optical Cavity section.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum mechanics is unitary, so for every process a reverse process also has to be possible, and that light can leave the cavity the same way it came in.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Optical Cavity
quotes: quantum mechanics has a property known as being unitary, in which for every process a reverse process also has to be possible
light can leave the cavity the same way it came in
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the property it uses to write each Hamiltonian.

assertions.value: The authors write the Hamiltonian of a cavity that light can enter or leave as a coupling term between the free photon and the cavity photon plus its reverse, with a constant c that sets the rate at which light enters the cavity.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Optical Cavity
quotes: The Hamiltonian of a cavity which light can enter or leave is therefore
where c c c is a constant describing the rate at which the light enters the cavity
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the model it uses in the Optical Cavity section.

assertions.value: The authors state that the time for the light to fully transfer into the cavity is inversely proportional to the constant c.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Optical Cavity
quotes: If we wait for the right amount of time, which is proportional to 1 / c 1/c 1/ c , then the light will fully transfer to the cavity.
assertions.reader_inference: The quote says the time is proportional to the reciprocal of c; the value restates that in words.

assertions.value: The authors state that in sum-frequency generation two light particles at specific frequencies combine to make one light particle at a frequency that is the sum of the two.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Sum-frequency Generation
quotes: two light particles at specific frequencies combine to make one light particle at a frequency that is the sum of the two
assertions.certainty_reason: The page defines the nonlinear process it uses.

assertions.value: The authors write the Hamiltonian of the sum-frequency process as the removal of photons s and i with creation of photon p, plus its reverse, with a constant G set by the material and the light intensity, and state that concentrating light into a small space makes the interaction stronger.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Sum-frequency Generation
quotes: The overall Hamiltonian that describes the processes that are allowed to happen is therefore
where G G G is a constant that relates to the material that is used to create the interactions and light intensity
Concentrating light into a small space makes the interaction stronger.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the model it uses in the Sum-frequency Generation section.

assertions.value: The authors state that if G is large compared to the rate at which the light can enter the cavity, the light will be prevented from entering.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Sum-frequency Generation
quotes: If G G G is large compared to the rate at which the light can enter the cavity
, then the light will be prevented from entering.
assertions.reader_inference: The page states this as a qualitative result; it gives no derivation at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the minimal model implicitly assumes the cavity is resonant with s, i and p, that this is difficult to engineer in practice but mathematically easier to describe, and that loss would otherwise have to be described, which would significantly complicate the equation.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: we are implicitly assuming it is resonant with all three. This is a situation that is difficult to engineer in practice, but mathematically easier to describe.
we would have to also mathematically describe loss from the cavity, which would significantly complicate our equation
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the assumption and its practical limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that with no light particle in the cavity the nonlinear terms cannot act, because there is no particle i or p, so the light particle enters the cavity unimpeded regardless of the size of G.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: In this case, the nonlinear effects do nothing because there are no particles i i i or p p p
Regardless of the size of G G G , the light particle will just enter the cavity unimpeded.

assertions.value: The authors state that when G and c are of comparable size, some light enters the cavity and some is converted to p, and the results are messy.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: Some light will enter the cavity and some will be converted to p p p , and the results will be messy.

assertions.value: The authors state that when the ratio of c to G is much greater than one in the presence of a light particle i, the nonlinear effects do little and the light particle just transfers into the cavity.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: then the nonlinear effects won't really do much of anything and the light particle will just transfer.

assertions.value: The authors state that when G is much larger than c and a light particle i is present, the amplitude cannot build up in i, so the light particle remains outside the cavity in f, and one light particle is bounced off another.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: , then we can have a Zeno blockade. The amplitude will not be able to build up in i i i so the light particle will have to remain outside the cavity in f f f .
This is exciting, because we can literally bounce one light particle off another.
assertions.reader_inference: The argument is qualitative; the page shows an animation (not in the text) and no quantitative calculation.

assertions.value: The authors state that each time the Hamiltonian changes a light particle the amplitude is multiplied by a factor, that converting into p and back therefore gives the amplitude a factor of minus one, and that the amplitudes coming directly from f cancel with those coming back from p, leaving the light outside the cavity.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: Therefore when the light gets converted into p p p and comes back, the amplitude has a factor of − 1 -1 − 1 .
The amplitudes coming directly from f f f cancel with those coming back from p p p , leaving the light outside of the cavity, and indeed causing the light particles to bounce off each other.
assertions.reader_inference: The page says the per-step factor is the square root of minus one and that two steps give minus one; this is the usual factor of i from the Schroedinger equation, but the page does not derive it.

assertions.value: The authors state that transferring into the cavity and back leads to a factor of minus one, and that this can be used to perform quantum logical operations known as quantum gates.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: transferring into the cavity and back will lead to a factor of − 1 -1 − 1
this can be used to perform quantum logical operations, known as quantum gates
assertions.reader_inference: No gate construction or fidelity is given on this page.

assertions.value: The authors state that in a more realistic case where p can be lost the mathematics are more complicated but the basic behavior is the same.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Simplified Zeno Blockade
quotes: In a more realistic case where p p p can be lost, the mathematics are more complicated, but the basic behavior is the same.
assertions.reader_inference: No calculation or reference is given on this page for the lossy case.

assertions.value: The authors state that the description on the page is highly simplified and meant to give a taste of the mathematics, and that in reality there are several complications.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: The description we have given here is highly simplified, intending to give a taste of the mathematics behind the effects.
In reality, there are several complications.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the scope of its own treatment.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simplified model does not account for the free photon f moving across a fiber with changing amplitude, nor for getting photon i into the cavity, and that pulse shaping can address these effects.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: our simplified mathematical description hasn't taken into account that light particle f f f will actually be moving across a fiber and will not have constant amplitude as it passes by
Issues related to these effects can be addressed by shaping the pulses of light

assertions.value: The authors state that it is hard in practice to make G large because the nonlinear effects are weak, and that the fields must be made strong by confining them to small regions of space.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: It is hard to make G G G large in practice since the nonlinear effects themselves are weak.
The fields need to be made strong by confining them to small regions of space.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states this as a limit of its own approach.

assertions.value: The authors state that their team has demonstrated Zeno blockade at the single photon level.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: Our team has made great progress though and has been able to demonstrate Zeno blockade at the single photon level
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer does not carry the link to the supporting publication, so the measurement is not checkable from this page.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear effects are stronger if more light particles are involved, but that the company's vision is to compute with few photons, so this is not an option for them.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: the nonlinear effects are stronger if more light particles are involved, but our vision is to compute with few photons , so this is not an option for us.

assertions.value: The authors state that the cavities need to be of very high quality so light particles are not lost, and that their team has made excellent cavities with lithium niobate.
assertions.anchor: Zeno Blockade page, Real Zeno Blockade
quotes: The cavities need to be very high quality so light particles aren't lost.
Our team has been able to make excellent cavities with lithium niobate.
assertions.reader_inference: No quality factor or loss figure is given on this page.
